CacheHit.name: CacheHit
CacheHit.description: Emitted when a program answers from a prior receipt instead of recomputing (spec §2.3).

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1).

fields.name: served_run
fields.description: The run whose receipt supplied the answer.

fields.name: receipt
fields.description: That receipt's path.

Command.name: Command
Command.description: A command's description: name, intent, declared effects, declared secrets and the message types it can emit (spec §4.1 to §4.3). Emitted by --schema and --help.

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1).

fields.name: intent
fields.description: One line: what question the command answers.

fields.name: secrets
fields.description: Arguments by flag, environment variables by name, and credential sources by logical name, whose values are secrets (spec §4.3, §5.3).

fields.name: emits
fields.description: Message types this command can emit, by exact (id, version).

fields.name: writes
fields.description: Subject-matter writes only (spec §4.3).

fields.name: bookkeeping
fields.description: Evidence writes: receipts, sidecars, the local ignore file, retention (spec §4.3).

End.name: End
End.description: The terminal event of a run that bootstrapped: written to stdout and to the receipt as one event. Its seq is the run's final sequence number (spec §3.3).

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1).

fields.name: status
fields.description: The exit status the process is about to exit with (spec §3.4); never 3, since a run that could not bootstrap has no end.

fields.name: receipt
fields.description: The receipt path, absolute, as the bootstrap line declared it.

fields.name: redacted
fields.description: True exactly when the head carries redacted or any redaction event was emitted (spec §3.3).

Error.name: Error
Error.description: Errors are data. measured, limit and remedy are what make an error actionable in one step rather than several.

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter; 0 is the bootstrap line (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to. Required on every line so a detached line can still be attributed (spec §1.3).

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stable identifier: two or more dot-separated segments of lowercase letters, digits and underscores (spec §6). Never a prose message.

fields.name: problem
fields.description: What is wrong, in one sentence.

fields.name: measured
fields.description: The value observed, when the failure is a threshold.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: The threshold that was not met.

fields.name: remedy
fields.description: The lever to pull. Omit rather than invent one.

fields.name: remedy_target
fields.description: What the remedy applies to.

fields.name: argv
fields.description: Indexes into argv.

fields.name: resolved
fields.description: JSON Pointers (RFC 6901) into resolved.

fields.name: env
fields.description: Names of declared environment variables that were present.

fields.name: inputs
fields.description: Indexes into inputs whose path carried a replaced value.

fields.name: sources
fields.description: Logical names of declared credential sources that were present (spec §5.3).

HistoryTransform.name: HistoryTransform
HistoryTransform.description: The opening line of a projected copy of a run on the shared history stream: every line of this run that follows on this stream is a projection of the receipt copy by the named transform, so a reader can tell a projected copy from a whole one and by what (spec §8, informative). Stream only: the receipt copy is never projected and never carries this line.

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3). This line takes a seq of its own and reaches no other sink, so the receipt copy has no line at this seq.

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution whose copy on this stream is a projection (spec §2.1).

fields.name: name
fields.description: What the transform is called: the name its configuration gave it, or the function's own name.

fields.name: sha256
fields.description: SHA-256, hex, of the transform's source text as the runtime renders it. It tells two projections apart and pins which one wrote this copy; it is not a build identity, and nothing fetches it.

fields.name: error
fields.description: Why the input could not be read; no digest then.

Lens.name: Lens
Lens.description: The lens a result carries: the asker, the view, the budget and the window that produced it, the query it answers, a stated bound on what the view loses, and the records it was built from by (run, seq) (spec §9, informative; decided in flyingrobots/parley#46). One lens line precedes the result it describes, so a later reader knows what it is looking at and can get back to the records.

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to: the read itself, not the runs being read (spec §2.1).

fields.name: session
fields.description: Working period spanning runs. Supplied by the caller or inherited; never invented (spec §2.1).

fields.name: query
fields.description: The recorded query this result answers, by (run, seq). Required: §9 records every query, and a result whose query was not recorded cannot be audited.

fields.name: asker
fields.description: Echoed from the query: who the result is for.

fields.name: view
fields.description: The view this result is. Echoed from the query, from the same closed set.

fields.name: budget
fields.description: The budget actually applied, including a default the query did not supply. Constitutive, not decoration: two results computed under different budgets are not comparable, so a lens without it does not identify the view that produced the result.

fields.name: window
fields.description: The stretch of history the result covers, echoed from the query.

fields.name: fold
fields.description: Echoed from the query, present exactly when the query states it (flyingrobots/parley#133). false: the read folded nothing, so loss.folded is 0 and no runs section carries folded because none was allowed to, not because no runs repeated. Two results over one window, one folded and one not, are not comparable, so a lens says which it is.

fields.name: loss
fields.description: What the view loses against the records it was built from, so a later reader knows which questions this result can still answer and cannot mistake a digest for the whole. A digest that folded runs names fewer records than it stands for, and says how many in folded.

fields.name: runs
fields.description: One section per run that records names, in the order records first names it, and none for any other run (flyingrobots/parley#83). It states once what is true of every record of the run — which invocation it was and what became of it — rather than on each entry. Read off the window's records when the lens is built, so it cannot drift from the head it summarises. Part of the line budget.bytes bounds. Optional so that lines written under the earlier drafts still validate; parley-read always writes it.

fields.name: records
fields.description: The records this result was built from, by (run, seq), never more than budget.records of them. Stored rather than recomputed: projecting down to a result is cheap and expanding back up may be impossible within a budget, so the way back has to be written here. A result is built from records, never from another result. Each entry may also carry a fixed summary of the record it names — event, t and, on an error or warning, its code — so a reader can choose what to open without opening it (flyingrobots/parley#77, flyingrobots/parley#83). What is true of the entry's whole run, its identity and outcome, is stated once in runs. The summary is read off the record when the lens is built and is part of the line budget.bytes bounds.

fields.name: bound
fields.description: What kind of statement the loss is. none: nothing in the window was left out, so the result and the window hold the same records and excluded must be 0. Not restricted to the identity view: a view orders a result and filters none of it (flyingrobots/parley#49), so any view whose result reached the end of its order lost nothing. count-only: the excluded count is all that is known, which is a weak proxy. A measured distortion bound needs a translator to measure it and is a later version of this schema.

fields.name: excluded
fields.description: How many records in the window the view did not name, whatever left them out: the budget, or a fold (folded). A proxy and a weak one: one withheld record can matter more than fifty, so this count cannot bound what the view loses.

fields.name: folded
fields.description: How many of excluded were left out because their run was folded into another run of the same invocation and the same result, rather than by the budget (flyingrobots/parley#79): the records of every run the fold left out. A runs section's folded.records counts those its own run stands for, so the sections' folded.records sum to this number unless the budget left a run that stands for others out of records; that run has no section, so the sum is then smaller and this count is all the lens says of its fold. It depends on the window, the view and fold, never on the budget, so excluded minus folded is what the budget cut. At most excluded, which a schema cannot check; a reader can. Optional so that lines written under the earlier drafts still validate; parley-read always writes it, 0 included.

MessageSchema.name: MessageSchema
MessageSchema.description: One message schema, carried by --schema and --help (spec §4.1, §4.2).

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1).

fields.name: schema
fields.description: The JSON Schema document for that exact (id, version).

Page.name: Page
Page.description: One page of unbounded output; cursor required when has_more is true (spec §7.2).

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1).

fields.name: cursor
fields.description: Opaque to the caller.

fields.name: tool
fields.description: The calling program, named as in spec §2.1. Established from the caller's own identity or supplied as one argument; never invented, so a read that cannot establish it is refused.

fields.name: cwd
fields.description: Absolute POSIX working directory the read was made from. Inferred from the process; omitted when it is not meaningful.

fields.name: task
fields.description: The caller's current task id, supplied by the caller and never inferred (flyingrobots/parley#61); omitted when the caller does not state it. Not the session: a session is a working period, a task is a unit of work inside one.

fields.name: records
fields.description: The most records the answer may name. Required: a view with no bound collapses into "return every record".

fields.name: bytes
fields.description: The most bytes the answer may occupy.

fields.name: ms
fields.description: The most wall-clock milliseconds the read may spend.

fields.name: from
fields.description: Inclusive lower bound of the window, POSIX time in milliseconds. 0 means "from the start of the history".

fields.name: to
fields.description: Inclusive upper bound of the window, POSIX time in milliseconds. Never below from.

ReadQuery.name: ReadQuery
ReadQuery.description: A read against the history, recorded as an event: the asker it is for, the view it wants, the budget it will accept and the window it covers (spec §9, informative; the representation is decided in flyingrobots/parley#46 and read against the observer-geometry treatment in docs/topics/related-work/observer-geometry.md). The envelope's run is the read's own run; asker is who the read is for. A drill-down, which opens records a lens named, is the same message with records stating which.

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to: the read itself, not the runs being read (spec §2.1).

fields.name: session
fields.description: Working period spanning runs. Supplied by the caller or inherited; never invented (spec §2.1).

fields.name: asker
fields.description: Who the read is for, and the context the budget is inferred from. The asker is not the view: two askers requesting the same view under the same budget get the same answer.

fields.name: view
fields.description: The shape of the answer, one token from a closed set. Never inferred: there is no privileged view, so a missing view is refused rather than guessed. Adding a token is a version of this schema.

fields.name: budget
fields.description: The size of answer the asker will accept. One documented default applies when it is not supplied, and the applied budget is carried verbatim by the result's lens, so a default is never invisible.

fields.name: window
fields.description: The stretch of history the read covers, always stated as two timestamps and echoed by the result's lens.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Free text from the asker, recorded and never parsed. Nothing in the answer branches on it.

fields.name: fold
fields.description: Whether the read may fold runs it judges to be repeats of one invocation with one result into the most recent of them (flyingrobots/parley#79). false: nothing is folded, so every run in the window keeps its own records and the budget alone decides what the answer names (flyingrobots/parley#133). true or absent: the reader folds, and the result's lens names the runs a fold stands for in the section of the run that stands for them (parley.lens runs.folded.stands_for). The budget can leave that run out of the answer, and its section with it; the lens then reports that fold as a count alone (parley.lens loss.folded). Never inferred: the reader records it only when the asker states it, and the lens echoes it. It selects nothing on a drill-down.

fields.name: records
fields.description: Present only on a drill-down: the records the read asks for by (run, seq), the identity a parley.lens names them by, in the order asked (flyingrobots/parley#51). A drill-down answers with exactly these records in full, a sidecar's stored record included, and an outcome per id; the view and window are recorded and select nothing, budget.records is the number of ids asked, and budget.bytes, when stated, bounds the records opened: whole records in the order asked while their summed size stays within it, and an over_budget outcome with no contents for each id past it (flyingrobots/parley#78). Absent on a read that answers with a digest.

ReceiptHead.name: ReceiptHead
ReceiptHead.description: First line of a receipt file. Carries what the bootstrap line deliberately omitted, so stdout stays small while the record stays complete.

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter continues from the bootstrap line, which is seq 0 (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1). ULID or equivalent: unique per execution and lexicographically sortable.

fields.name: tool
fields.description: The program that wrote this receipt, so a receipt read alone says what produced it (spec §5).

fields.name: v
fields.description: That program's own version; with tool, a component of the inv preimage (spec §2.2) that a receipt read alone must carry.

fields.name: inv
fields.description: Content-addressed identity of the question (spec §2.2); never includes a declared secret. Optional in v0.2: supplied when the tool documents its derivation and the identity is known at this point; never a placeholder (spec §2.2).

fields.name: argv
fields.description: As received, after §5.3 redaction: a declared secret appears as the literal [redacted].

fields.name: resolved
fields.description: After defaults, environment and path resolution. The gap between this and argv is where bugs live.

fields.name: inputs
fields.description: Every declared input as a descriptor: its path, its role when the tool distinguishes roles, and a content digest once read. A digest that arrives later is carried by receipt.inputs (spec §2.2). Credential files are never inputs (§2.2).

fields.name: redacted
fields.description: Present and non-empty whenever a declared secret was supplied to the run; absent otherwise (spec §5.3). Lists where the head carries a replaced value, and which credential sources were present.

fields.name: dry_run
fields.description: True when the run performed no subject-matter writes, no mutating remote action and no retention deletion (spec §4.3). Absent means false.

ReceiptInputs.name: ReceiptInputs
ReceiptInputs.description: The metadata-finalisation record: late input digests and, when known, inv; emitted once inputs are settled and before end (spec §2.2).

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1).

fields.name: inputs
fields.description: Every declared input as a descriptor: its path, its role when the tool distinguishes roles, and a content digest once read. A digest that arrives later is carried by receipt.inputs (spec §2.2). Credential files are never inputs (§2.2).

fields.name: inv
fields.description: Present when the identity could be computed (spec §2.2).

fields.name: receipt
fields.description: Absolute path of the receipt file for this run (spec §5). The only path the protocol defines; a program may add others it documents.

ReceiptStep.name: ReceiptStep
ReceiptStep.description: One decision the program made while working, with its reason; receipt only (spec §5).

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: 0 for a bootstrap or startup-failure line (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: 0 for a bootstrap or startup-failure line (spec §1.3).

fields.name: event
fields.description: The named record's event token as the loader read it, a tool's own token included verbatim (flyingrobots/parley#77). Absent when the record carries none; never filled in.

fields.name: t
fields.description: The named record's POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3) as the loader read it. Absent when the record has no usable t; never a made-up one.

fields.name: code
fields.description: On an error or warning entry, the record's code (spec §6), so failures of one case read as one without opening them (flyingrobots/parley#83). Absent on any other record, and on a code that is not spec §6's shape; never filled in.

Redaction.name: Redaction
Redaction.description: A receipt line recording a redaction not covered by the head's redacted field: in the head itself (in: 1) or in any later record or sidecar (spec §5.3).

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1).

fields.name: in
fields.description: The seq of the affected record: the head, a result, an error, a reasoning line, or the stored record a sidecar holds (its source).

fields.name: at
fields.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) within that record.

RunBootstrap.name: RunBootstrap
RunBootstrap.description: First line of stdout, emitted before work begins so a crashed run still names its receipt.

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The bootstrap line is always the first line the run emits, so it is the only line with a pinned seq.

fields.name: v
fields.description: The program's own version, distinct from _schema.version on the same line (spec §3).

fields.name: inv
fields.description: Content-addressed identity of the question: tool, version, normalised args, and the bytes of every declared input; never a declared secret (spec §2.2, §5.3). Optional in v0.2: supplied when the tool documents its derivation and the identity is known at this point; never a placeholder (spec §2.2).

fields.name: run
fields.description: Unique, lexicographically sortable identity of this execution.

fields.name: session
fields.description: Working period spanning runs. Supplied by the caller or inherited.

fields.name: paths
fields.description: Files this run writes.

fields.name: dry_run
fields.description: True when the run performed no subject-matter writes, no mutating remote action and no retention deletion (spec §4.3). Absent means false.

fields.name: others
fields.description: How many other runs this section stands for, this run excluded: the section reads as this run plus others like it, so it stands for others + 1 runs (flyingrobots/parley#100).

fields.name: records
fields.description: How many records of those other runs, in the window, the fold left out of records, this run's own excluded; each is counted in loss.excluded and loss.folded.

fields.name: stands_for
fields.description: The run ids of the other runs this section stands for, this run excluded, most recent first by the rule that makes this run the most recent of them: the latest t among each run's records in the window, then the greater run id, a run with no dated record last (flyingrobots/parley#133). It names runs, not records: the others' seq numbers are not listed and need not be this run's, so their records are read under a window that holds them with fold false, or opened by (run, seq) once their seq is known. As many as others, which a schema cannot check; a reader can. Optional, as every field a minor version adds is (spec §4.5); parley-read always writes it, never shortens it, never drops it to fit the section's bound and does not count it against that bound. It is part of the line budget.bytes bounds: when the line cannot hold it whole, no record of this run is named and this section is absent, and loss.folded still counts the fold.

fields.name: run
fields.description: The run this section is about: one that records names.

fields.name: tool
fields.description: The run's receipt head's tool (spec §5), as the loader read it.

fields.name: v
fields.description: The run's receipt head's v (spec §5), as the loader read it.

fields.name: argv
fields.description: The run's receipt head's argv (spec §5), already redacted there (spec §5.3). Never cut part-way: when it does not fit the section's bound it is dropped whole and named in dropped.

fields.name: resolved
fields.description: The run's receipt head's resolved (spec §5): its interpretation after defaults, environment and path resolution, copied whole and already redacted there (spec §5.3), so a reader can tell, say, which commits a run compared without opening the head (flyingrobots/parley#90). Its shape is the tool's; the reader chooses none of its keys. Never cut part-way: when it does not fit the section's bound it is dropped whole, first of all fields, and named in dropped. Absent when the window does not hold the head or the head's resolved is not an object.

fields.name: inv
fields.description: The run's inv (spec §2.2): the head's, or else the window's receipt.inputs for the run. Absent when neither carries one; never a placeholder.

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: What the records in the window establish about the run: failed for an error, a startup failure or a non-zero end; succeeded for an end of 0 and nothing against it; undetermined otherwise (spec §1.2a). It is the window's verdict, not the digest's: a run whose end the bound cut is still succeeded. Absent when the reader established none.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Why the outcome is undetermined, present exactly when it is. no_end_in_window: the window holds no end for the run, which cannot say whether the run ended later or never did. end_status_unusable: the window holds an end whose status is not a number.

fields.name: head
fields.description: Present when the window does not hold the run's receipt head, so tool, v and argv are not known from it. Absent when it does.

fields.name: folded
fields.description: Present when this run stands for other runs of the same invocation and the same result (flyingrobots/parley#79): runs with an equal inv (spec §2.2) whose outcome, reason, end status, error, warning and startup-failure codes and head's resolved are equal too, and whose result records are equal one for one in seq order: the tool's own records and any other record the protocol does not define, each page, each sidecar by its bytes and sha256, and a read's own lens without its session and the query it names, compared without the envelope's t, seq and run (flyingrobots/parley#133). A top-level session on a record of the tool's own or on a page is that record's own field and is compared (flyingrobots/parley#146). Under a view whose surface holds decision records those are equal as well, compared the same way: receipt.step under how-it-decided and everything, cache.hit under those two and what-ran. A decision record of a kind the view's surface does not hold is not compared, so runs that differ only in such records still stand for one another. Every comparison here is of the records the window holds: two runs whose results in the window differ are a divergence (spec §2.3) and do not stand for one another, and a run only partly inside the window is compared by the part the window holds, so runs that stand for one another under one window can differ under a wider one. A section marks a run the window did not hold whole in two cases: head not_in_window when the window does not hold the run's head, and outcome undetermined with reason no_end_in_window when it holds no end for the run and no failure either; a run the window shows to have failed is failed with or without its end, so its section does not say whether the window holds the end. This run is the most recent of them, by the latest t among each run's records in the window and, where those are equal, the greater run id; the others' records are not named, and stands_for lists the others' run ids. A run with no inv in the window, a run the window shows to be redacted (its head carries redacted, an end in the window states redacted true, or the window holds a redaction event of the run), and a run the window does not show to be unredacted, because it holds neither the run's receipt head nor an end that states redacted false, do not stand for another (spec §1.2a, §2.3). A run that stands for no other has no folded. Never dropped to fit the section's bound.

fields.name: dropped
fields.description: The fields left out, whole, to bound the section's serialised JSON, in the order they were dropped, each at most once: resolved, then argv, then inv, then v, then tool. The bound is the reader's to state (parley-read: 512 UTF-8 bytes); a string or an object is never cut part-way.

fields.name: version
fields.description: Full validation is against the schema for this exact id and version (spec §4.5, §4.6).

Sidecar.name: Sidecar
Sidecar.description: A receipt line standing in for a record stored beside the receipt because it exceeded the inline threshold (spec §5).

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to (spec §2.1).

fields.name: source
fields.description: The seq of the record the sidecar holds.

fields.name: path
fields.description: Relative to the receipt's directory; never absolute, never escaping it.

fields.name: bytes
fields.description: Length of the stored bytes.

fields.name: sha256
fields.description: SHA-256 of the stored bytes; not the semantic digest of §7.1.

StartupFailed.name: StartupFailed
StartupFailed.description: The single line a run emits, on stderr, when it cannot reach the bootstrap line; exit status 3 (spec §3.2).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The only line the run emits (spec §1.3, §3.2).

fields.name: code
fields.description: A §6 code in the startup namespace.

Warning.name: Warning
Warning.description: A recovered condition: the same shape as an error, on stderr and in the receipt, never changing the exit status (spec §6.1).

fields.name: t
fields.description: POSIX time in milliseconds (spec §1.3).

fields.name: seq
fields.description: The run's single counter; 0 is the bootstrap line (spec §1.3).

fields.name: run
fields.description: The execution this line belongs to. Required on every line so a detached line can still be attributed (spec §1.3).

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stable identifier: two or more dot-separated segments of lowercase letters, digits and underscores (spec §6). Never a prose message.

fields.name: problem
fields.description: What is wrong, in one sentence.

fields.name: measured
fields.description: The value observed, when the failure is a threshold.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: The threshold that was not met.

fields.name: remedy
fields.description: The lever to pull. Omit rather than invent one.

fields.name: remedy_target
fields.description: What the remedy applies to.
